boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Amherst College
boards.description: A guide to the essential late-night food stops for Amherst College students, featuring on-campus staples and downtown favorites that stay open for the late-night study grind.

cards.title: Late Night at Val
cards.subtitle: Amherst College Dining
cards.notes: Visit the downstairs area of the main dining hall for late-night snacks like mozzarella sticks and fries during the academic year.
cards.short_summary: The primary on-campus late-night dining option located within the main student dining commons.
cards.evidence_claim: Valentine Hall offers a 'Late Night' service from 9:30 PM to 11:00 PM, Sunday through Thursday, during the traditional academic year.
cards.source_title: Valentine Hall | Dining Location Hours - Amherst College
cards.access_notes: Open to students with a valid meal plan; hours are typically 9:30 PM - 11:00 PM Sunday-Thursday.

cards.title: Science Center Late Bites
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Study Fuel
cards.notes: Head to the Science Center atrium for late-night coffee and snacks in one of the campus's newest and most popular study spaces.
cards.short_summary: A modern cafe located in the Science Center that serves as a late-night alternative for students.
cards.evidence_claim: The Science Center Cafe offers late-night food options until 10:00 PM on weeknights during the academic semester.
cards.source_title: Schwemm's Transformed into Merchandise Store - The Amherst Student
cards.access_notes: Open until 10:00 PM on weeknights; accessible to the campus community.

cards.title: Antonio's Pizza Slices
cards.subtitle: Downtown Pizza Staple
cards.notes: Grab a signature slice like Potato Bacon or Tortellini at this legendary downtown spot that stays busy well past midnight.
cards.short_summary: A famous downtown Amherst pizzeria known for its diverse and creative pizza-by-the-slice options.
cards.evidence_claim: Antonio's Pizza is open until 2:00 AM daily, serving as a primary late-night destination for the Amherst community.
cards.source_title: Antonio's Pizza | Restaurants | Catering | Dining - Amherst Area Chamber of Commerce
cards.access_notes: Open until 2:00 AM every night for walk-in slice service.

cards.title: Insomnia Cookies
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Cookie Delivery
cards.notes: Order warm cookies or ice cream sandwiches for delivery or pickup until the early morning hours.
cards.short_summary: A bakery specializing in warm cookies delivered late into the night, located just off campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Insomnia Cookies in Amherst is open for pickup and delivery until 3:00 AM daily.
cards.source_title: 93 - Insomnia Cookies | Newsroom
cards.access_notes: Open until 3:00 AM daily for both in-store pickup and delivery.

cards.title: Wings Over Amherst
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Wing Delivery
cards.notes: A go-to for late-night delivery of boneless wings and fries, especially popular during weekend study breaks.
cards.short_summary: A popular chicken wing chain known for its late-night delivery service to the local colleges.
cards.evidence_claim: Wings Over Amherst is open until 2:00 AM on Thursday, Friday, and Saturday nights.
cards.source_title: Amherst MA Late Night Guide: What's Open After 9 PM
cards.access_notes: Open until 2:00 AM Thursday-Saturday; delivery is a primary service for students.

cards.title: Cumberland Farms 24/7
cards.subtitle: Round-the-Clock Essentials
cards.notes: Stop by for 24-hour access to snacks, coffee, and basic groceries when everything else in town is closed.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour convenience store and gas station that serves as a reliable late-night resource.
cards.evidence_claim: The Cumberland Farms location at 35 Belchertown Rd in Amherst is open 24 hours a day.
cards.source_title: amherst, ma , (413) 256-8332 - Cumberland Farms
cards.access_notes: Open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.

cards.title: Royal Chicken & Kebab
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Mediterranean
cards.notes: Visit this Boltwood Walk spot for late-night kebabs, gyros, and fried chicken in the heart of downtown.
cards.short_summary: A Mediterranean eatery offering late-night dining options in downtown Amherst.
cards.evidence_claim: Royal Chicken & Kebab is open until 2:00 AM from Thursday through Sunday.
cards.source_title: Amherst MA Late Night Guide: What's Open After 9 PM
cards.access_notes: Open until 2:00 AM Thursday-Sunday; midnight on other days.

cards.title: Papa Johns Late Delivery
cards.subtitle: Reliable Late-Night Pizza
cards.notes: A standard choice for late-night pizza delivery when campus dining has closed for the evening.
cards.short_summary: A national pizza chain providing late-night delivery services to the Amherst area.
cards.evidence_claim: Papa Johns in Amherst is open until 2:00 AM Sunday-Thursday and 3:00 AM Friday-Saturday.
cards.source_title: Amherst MA Late Night Guide: What's Open After 9 PM
cards.access_notes: Delivery and carryout available until 2:00 AM or 3:00 AM depending on the day.

cards.title: Taco Bell Late Night
cards.subtitle: Fast Food Run
cards.notes: A short drive to Hadley provides access to the late-night 'Fourth Meal' menu for students with cars.
cards.short_summary: A nearby fast-food option in Hadley that stays open late for Mexican-inspired snacks.
cards.evidence_claim: The Taco Bell in Hadley is open until 1:00 AM daily for late-night orders.
cards.source_title: Amherst MA Late Night Guide: What's Open After 9 PM
cards.access_notes: Open until 1:00 AM daily; located a few miles from campus in Hadley.

cards.title: Dunkin' on College St
cards.subtitle: Early Morning Coffee
cards.notes: While not 24 hours, this location opens very early for students pulling all-nighters or heading to early practices.
cards.short_summary: A local Dunkin' location that serves as an early morning or late evening coffee stop.
cards.evidence_claim: The Dunkin' at 312 College St in Amherst opens at 5:00 AM daily to serve early morning commuters and students.
cards.source_title: Dunkin' at 312 College St in Amherst | Coffee & Donuts Near You
cards.access_notes: Opens at 5:00 AM daily; useful for the very end of a late-night study session.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Discover the functional student-preferred spots at Amherst College, from silent library levels to late-night gathering hubs and scenic campus retreats.

cards.title: The Catacombs
cards.subtitle: Robert Frost Library
cards.notes: Head to the lowest level for absolute silence. Known as the 'Catacombs,' this floor is the go-to for students needing to 'lock-in' for intense, distraction-free study sessions.
cards.short_summary: The silent basement level of Frost Library preferred for intense individual study.
cards.evidence_claim: Level C of Frost Library is known as the 'catacombs' and is a designated silent zone popular for productive, long-duration studying.
cards.source_title: Current Favorite Study Spots on Campus – Amherst College Admission Student Blogs
cards.access_notes: Open during library hours; Level C is a designated silent zone.

cards.title: Late Night at Schwemm's
cards.subtitle: Keefe Campus Center
cards.notes: Visit for late-night food and a social atmosphere. It features a fireplace and computer stations, serving as a central gathering spot for students after hours.
cards.short_summary: A social coffeehouse in the campus center known for late-night dining and student hangouts.
cards.evidence_claim: Schwemm's Coffee House in Keefe Campus Center is a central spot for late-night eats and social hangouts, open until midnight on weekends.
cards.source_title: Student Engagement & Leadership | Keefe Campus Center - Amherst College
cards.access_notes: Open until 11 PM Sun-Wed and 12 AM Thu-Sat during the academic year.

cards.title: Study Among the Fossils
cards.subtitle: Beneski Building
cards.notes: Find a table on the museum floors for a 'mid-social' study environment. The ambient noise is low, and you are surrounded by dinosaur tracks and Ice Age megafauna.
cards.short_summary: Quiet study areas located within the galleries of the natural history museum.
cards.evidence_claim: The Beneski Museum is cited by students as a 'mid-social' study spot where they can work surrounded by natural history exhibits.
cards.source_title: Ranking Study Spots – Amherst College Admission Student Blogs
cards.access_notes: Available during museum public hours; quiet behavior is required near classrooms.

cards.title: The Powerhouse
cards.subtitle: East Campus
cards.notes: Check out this repurposed steam plant for student-run performances and parties. It also opens 24/7 as a study hall during reading and final exam periods.
cards.short_summary: A versatile student event space in a converted industrial building used for social events and late-night study.
cards.evidence_claim: The Powerhouse is a student gathering space for performances and social events, and it provides 24/7 access for study during exam periods.
cards.source_title: The Eighmy Powerhouse | Hours - Amherst College
cards.access_notes: Open for scheduled events; 24/7 access during finals for students.

cards.title: Tuttle Hill Farm
cards.subtitle: Tuttle Hill
cards.notes: Walk up the hill to visit the student-centered farm. It hosts social events and a weekly farm stand on the quad, providing fresh produce grown right on campus.
cards.short_summary: The campus farm where students work, visit for events, and source local produce.
cards.evidence_claim: Book & Plow Farm is a student-centered operation on Tuttle Hill that hosts social events and provides vegetables for the dining hall.
cards.source_title: Sustainability Academics - Book & Plow Farm - Amherst College
cards.access_notes: Open for student visits and scheduled farm events.

cards.title: Sanctuary Trail Network
cards.subtitle: South Campus
cards.notes: Explore 500 acres of woods and wetlands. The trails are used by students for exercise, research, and quiet reflection away from the main campus bustle.
cards.short_summary: A large forested preserve with trails for recreation and environmental research.
cards.evidence_claim: The Wildlife Sanctuary includes 500 acres of trails and is used by students for personal reflection, exercise, and research.
cards.source_title: Recreation: Trails & Points of Interest | Wildlife Sanctuary - Amherst College
cards.access_notes: Open to the public for trail use during daylight hours.

cards.title: The Mead Galleries
cards.subtitle: Mead Art Museum
cards.notes: Study in a bright, colorful environment surrounded by art. It is open late on several weeknights, offering a quiet alternative to the library for focused work.
cards.short_summary: An art museum offering quiet study spaces within its galleries during evening hours.
cards.evidence_claim: The Mead Art Museum is open until midnight on select nights and is used by students as a quiet study space surrounded by artwork.
cards.source_title: Underappreciated Study Spots In and Around Amherst
cards.access_notes: Open until midnight on Sunday and Tuesday through Thursday nights.

cards.title: The Science Commons
cards.subtitle: Science Center
cards.notes: Gather in the large, glass-enclosed atrium for social studying. It is a high-energy spot with plenty of natural light and proximity to the campus cafe.
cards.short_summary: A modern, sunlit commons area in the Science Center popular for group work and socializing.
cards.evidence_claim: The Science Center's main commons is a popular gathering space for students and faculty, described as a 'most social' study spot.
cards.source_title: The Science Center - Amherst College
cards.access_notes: Open during building hours; highly social atmosphere.

cards.title: The Lone Steeple
cards.subtitle: Near Mead Art Museum
cards.notes: Visit this 150-foot monument, the only remains of a 19th-century church. Its nine bells still chime for major college events like Commencement and inaugurations.
cards.short_summary: A historic freestanding steeple that serves as a campus landmark and ceremonial bell tower.
cards.evidence_claim: Stearns Steeple is a freestanding structure remaining from the dismantled Stearns Church; its bells chime for college occasions.
cards.source_title: Stearns Steeple in Amherst - Atlas Obscura
cards.access_notes: Outdoor monument accessible 24/7; interior access is restricted.

cards.title: The Octagon
cards.subtitle: Gerald Penny '77 Center
cards.notes: Visit this historic 1848 building, now home to the Gerald Penny '77 Center. It hosts cultural programming and student organization meetings in a unique architectural setting.
cards.short_summary: A historic octagonal building used for student cultural events and meetings.
cards.evidence_claim: The Octagon houses the Gerald Penny '77 Center and is used for student cultural programming and meetings.
cards.source_title: Reservations and Facilities | Planning an Event - Amherst College
cards.access_notes: Accessible for scheduled student organization events and meetings.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Discover free social spaces and activities at Amherst College, from world-class museums and historic landmarks to late-night study hubs and nature trails.

cards.title: Browse Global Art Collections
cards.subtitle: 41 Quadrangle Drive
cards.notes: Explore over 20,000 artworks spanning thousands of years. Admission is free for everyone, and the study room offers a quiet space to view art up close.
cards.short_summary: A campus art museum with free public admission and a diverse global collection.
cards.evidence_claim: The Mead Art Museum offers free public admission six days a week.
cards.source_title: Mead Art Museum - Amherst College
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday–Sunday; closed Mondays. Public access is free.

cards.title: See Ice Age Megafauna
cards.subtitle: 11 Barrett Hill Drive
cards.notes: Walk through three floors of exhibits featuring dinosaur tracks and fossil skeletons. It is one of New England's largest natural history museums and always free.
cards.short_summary: A large natural history museum on campus with free admission for all visitors.
cards.evidence_claim: The Beneski Museum offers free admission to visitors of all ages, year-round.
cards.source_title: Beneski Museum of Natural History - Amherst College
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday–Friday 10AM-4PM, Saturday–Sunday 10AM-5PM.

cards.title: Catch the Holyoke Range View
cards.subtitle: South end of Main Quad
cards.notes: Relax in Adirondack chairs and enjoy panoramic views of the Holyoke Range. This iconic spot is a central gathering place for students to hang out between classes.
cards.short_summary: A scenic campus landmark known for its expansive mountain views and outdoor seating.
cards.evidence_claim: The War Memorial, with its view of the Holyoke Range, is a central location on our campus.
cards.source_title: Visiting - Amherst College
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7 as a public outdoor campus space.

cards.title: Study in the 24-Hour Atrium
cards.subtitle: 25 East Drive
cards.notes: Utilize the modern, sun-drenched atrium for group projects or late-night sessions. The building is technically open 24/7 for student use and features large whiteboards.
cards.short_summary: A modern academic building with a large atrium open 24 hours for student study.
cards.evidence_claim: A popular study spot is the Science Center, which is open 24 hours.
cards.source_title: Your Guide to Study Spots at Amherst | October
cards.access_notes: Open 24 hours for students; public access typically during business hours.

cards.title: Pick Your Own Flowers
cards.subtitle: 425 South East Street
cards.notes: Visit the farm on Tuttle Hill to pick wildflowers when in bloom during late summer. Community members are welcome to enjoy the grounds and Adirondack chairs.
cards.short_summary: A student-centered farm offering free flower picking and outdoor relaxation space.
cards.evidence_claim: Once it does [bloom], all campus community members are encouraged to come to the farm and pick flowers.
cards.source_title: Book & Plow Farm | Sustainability - Amherst College
cards.access_notes: Flower picking typically begins in late July. Grounds are open for visits anytime.

cards.title: Hike the Sanctuary Trails
cards.subtitle: South of College Street
cards.notes: Walk the Pond Loop or other wooded trails to spot local birds and vernal pools. The sanctuary features flat cross-country paths accessible from the campus edge.
cards.short_summary: A network of nature trails on college land open for hiking and birdwatching.
cards.evidence_claim: The campus map includes tours of each of the Sanctuary trails that you can follow along as you walk.
cards.source_title: Wildlife Sanctuary | Town & Valley - Amherst College
cards.access_notes: Open daily from dawn to dusk. Trail maps are available online.

cards.title: Watch Free Weekly Movies
cards.subtitle: 16 Barrett Hill Drive
cards.notes: Head to the campus theater for 'Flicks on Fleek,' a weekly screening of popular films. These events are free for Amherst students and provide a fun social break.
cards.short_summary: A student center theater hosting free weekly film screenings for the college community.
cards.evidence_claim: The Campus Center Theater is host to Flicks on Fleek, an activity that provides a popular film weekly at no charge to Amherst students.
cards.source_title: Keefe Campus Center Spaces | Reservations and Facilities - Amherst College
cards.access_notes: Screenings are typically held weekly during the academic year.

cards.title: Visit the Freestanding Steeple
cards.subtitle: Next to Mead Art Museum
cards.notes: Admire this 150-foot Gothic Revival monument, the only remains of the 1870 College Church. It stands as a historic landmark between James and Stearns Halls.
cards.short_summary: A historic 19th-century church steeple preserved as a freestanding campus monument.
cards.evidence_claim: In 1949 the church was dismantled... but the steeple remained as a monument.
cards.source_title: Stearns Steeple in Amherst - Atlas Obscura
cards.access_notes: Visible and accessible from the public quadrangle 24/7.

cards.title: Tour the Poet's Homestead
cards.subtitle: 280 Main Street
cards.notes: Amherst College students receive free admission to the home of Emily Dickinson. Explore the Homestead and The Evergreens to learn about her life and revolutionary poetry.
cards.short_summary: The historic home of poet Emily Dickinson, offering free tours to Amherst students.
cards.evidence_claim: Admission is free for all Amherst College students, faculty, and staff.
cards.source_title: Hours & Admission - Emily Dickinson Museum
cards.access_notes: Open March–December; advance timed-entry reservations are recommended.

cards.title: Hang Out in the Late-Night Hub
cards.subtitle: 61 Quadrangle Drive
cards.notes: Gather with friends for late-night study sessions in the 'dark academia' atmosphere. The library stays open until 1 AM most weeknights for student use.
cards.short_summary: The main campus library offering late-night study spaces and social areas for students.
cards.evidence_claim: Frost's hours are currently between 8 a.m. and 1 a.m. on weekdays.
cards.source_title: Frost Should Be Open 24/7 - The Amherst Student
cards.access_notes: Open until 1 AM Sunday–Thursday during the academic year.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: From the silent 'Catacombs' to sun-drenched museum reading rooms, these ten distinct environments offer the best physical affordances for focused academic work at Amherst College.

cards.title: The Catacombs
cards.subtitle: Silent Zone on the lowest level of Frost Library
cards.notes: Enter the lowest level for absolute silence. This floor features individual cubicles and large tables designed for deep, uninterrupted focus during long study sessions.
cards.short_summary: The 'Catacombs' is the designated silent study floor on the lowest level of Frost Library, featuring individual carrels.
cards.evidence_claim: Level C is a Silent Zone, with self-enforced silence for individual study, often referred to by students as the catacombs.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces & Room Reservations | Library - Amherst College
cards.access_notes: Open during library hours; typically 8 a.m. to 1 a.m. on weekdays during the academic year.

cards.title: The Living Room
cards.subtitle: Sun-drenched atrium in the Science Center
cards.notes: Utilize the large vaulted atrium with floor-to-ceiling windows. It offers a mix of colorful lounge seating and tables suitable for collaborative group work.
cards.short_summary: The Science Center Commons is a modern, light-filled atrium featuring open study areas and a cafe.
cards.evidence_claim: The Science Center offers a large and functional main commons with abundant light and open design for casual interaction and study.
cards.source_title: The Science Center - Amherst College
cards.access_notes: The building is technically open 24/7 for students with ID card access.

cards.title: The Dinosaur View
cards.subtitle: Second floor of the Beneski Museum of Natural History
cards.notes: Study among fossils in this second-floor room. It features old-fashioned furnishings and large windows overlooking the Science Center and the museum interior.
cards.short_summary: A quiet reading room located on the second floor of the Beneski Museum, offering views of the natural history exhibits.
cards.evidence_claim: The reading room on the second floor of Beneski has a perfect mix of views and aesthetics, with a sight of the Science Center and inside the museum.
cards.source_title: My Ranking of Known and Lesser-Known Study Spots Around Campus - Amherst College
cards.access_notes: Available during museum public hours; typically 11 a.m. to 4 p.m. Tuesday-Sunday.

cards.title: The Keefe Lounges
cards.subtitle: Non-reservable study rooms in the student union
cards.notes: Find these two dedicated sitting rooms for a more social study environment. They are available whenever the building is open and do not require reservations.
cards.short_summary: Two non-reservable sitting rooms in the Keefe Campus Center provide a convenient space for casual studying.
cards.evidence_claim: The two sitting rooms in the Keefe Campus Center are an ideal space for students to study in and are available whenever the center is open.
cards.source_title: Keefe Campus Center Spaces | Reservations and Facilities - Amherst College
cards.access_notes: Open 9 a.m. to 11 p.m. Sun-Wed, and until 12 a.m. Thu-Sat during the academic year.

cards.title: Arms Music Study
cards.subtitle: Second floor of the Arms Music Center
cards.notes: Access open study areas with tables surrounded by music scores and recordings. This space is typically quieter than the main library and offers specialized equipment.
cards.short_summary: A specialized library in the Arms Music Center offering quiet table seating and music-specific resources.
cards.evidence_claim: The Music Library has open study areas with tables available to all users whenever the library is open.
cards.source_title: Music Library | Spaces & Technology - Amherst College
cards.access_notes: Hours vary by semester; check the library website for current daily schedules.

cards.title: The 17th-Century Parlor
cards.subtitle: Historic oak-paneled room in the Mead Art Museum
cards.notes: Study in a 17th-century English knight's parlor. This oak-paneled room provides a unique, quiet atmosphere surrounded by historic architecture and art.
cards.short_summary: A historic, wood-paneled room within the Mead Art Museum used as a quiet study and event space.
cards.evidence_claim: The Mead Art Museum features a 17th-century English knight's parlor, the Rotherwas Room, which is a popular quiet study spot.
cards.source_title: Mead Art Museum - Amherst College
cards.access_notes: Open during museum hours: 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. Tuesday-Sunday.

cards.title: The Powerhouse
cards.subtitle: Multi-purpose student space in a converted plant
cards.notes: Take advantage of the 24/7 access during reading and exam periods. This converted power plant features comfortable lounge furniture and numerous work tables.
cards.short_summary: A former power plant converted into a student event and study space with a flexible, industrial layout.
cards.evidence_claim: The Powerhouse is equipped with comfortable lounge furniture and numerous tables, making it a great spot for work or study.
cards.source_title: The Eighmy Powerhouse | Hours - Amherst College
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7 for student access specifically during Reading Period and Final Exam Period.

cards.title: The Math Tower
cards.subtitle: Top floor of the Mathematics and CS building
cards.notes: Head to the fifth floor for a fantastic view of the campus. This area includes tables for doing work and is located near faculty offices in the tower section.
cards.short_summary: The top floor of Seelye Mudd offers quiet study tables and panoramic views of the Amherst campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The fifth floor of Seelye Mudd has a fantastic view of the campus and is a great place to work.
cards.source_title: Amherst's Hidden Gems (On-Campus Edition)
cards.access_notes: Accessible during building hours; typically requires ID card for late-night entry.

cards.title: The Aesthetic Gem
cards.subtitle: Cozy lounge located within Chapin Hall
cards.notes: Relax on comfortable couches in this plant-filled room. It features fairy lights and a collection of books, making it ideal for low-intensity reading or group meetings.
cards.short_summary: A cozy, aesthetic lounge in Chapin Hall known for its comfortable seating and relaxed atmosphere.
cards.evidence_claim: Pemberton Lounge is filled with books, plants, fairy lights, and the comfiest couches on campus.
cards.source_title: Amherst's Hidden Gems (On-Campus Edition)
cards.access_notes: Open during academic building hours; can be reserved for student group activities.

cards.title: Webster Hall View
cards.subtitle: Second floor of Webster Hall
cards.notes: Study in a room filled with hundreds of books and art. The second-floor location in Webster Hall provides one of the most elevated views of the campus quad.
cards.short_summary: A quiet academic center in Webster Hall featuring a library and significant views of the campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Center for Russian Culture on the second floor of Webster Hall has one of the best views of campus and a bunch of tables for doing work.
cards.source_title: Amherst's Hidden Gems (On-Campus Edition)
cards.access_notes: Open during standard academic hours; check the center's specific schedule for public access.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Explore the essential streets and corridors surrounding Amherst College, from the historic town common to the student-frequented hubs of downtown Amherst.

cards.title: The Town Common Gateway
cards.subtitle: South Pleasant Street Corridor
cards.notes: Walk along the town common to visit the Amherst Area Chamber of Commerce or grab a quick bite at Fresh Side.
cards.short_summary: A primary commercial corridor bordering the Amherst College campus and the historic town common.
cards.evidence_claim: South Pleasant Street is home to the Amherst Area Chamber of Commerce and various local eateries like Fresh Side.
cards.source_title: Business Directory Search - Amherst Area Chamber of Commerce
cards.access_notes: Public street accessible 24/7; business hours vary.

cards.title: The Downtown Dining Hub
cards.subtitle: North Pleasant Street Corridor
cards.notes: Head here for student favorites like Panda East or to visit the UMass Downtown welcome center.
cards.short_summary: The central commercial spine of downtown Amherst featuring a high concentration of student-oriented dining.
cards.evidence_claim: North Pleasant Street hosts numerous restaurants including Panda East and the UMass Downtown center at 108 N. Pleasant St.
cards.source_title: UMass Downtown
cards.access_notes: Public street; UMass Downtown is open during standard business hours.

cards.title: Historic Town Center
cards.subtitle: Main Street Corridor
cards.notes: Visit the historic Amherst Town Hall or stop by the Amherst Chinese Food restaurant for a meal.
cards.short_summary: A historic east-west corridor intersecting the town center with local government and dining landmarks.
cards.evidence_claim: Main Street features the Amherst Town Hall and long-standing businesses like Amherst Chinese Food.
cards.source_title: Town Hall | Amherst, MA - Official Website
cards.access_notes: Public street; Town Hall typically open weekdays 8:00 AM - 4:30 PM.

cards.title: The Community Courtyard
cards.subtitle: Boltwood Walk Block
cards.notes: Explore this pedestrian-friendly block to find Johnny's Tavern and the Bangs Community Center.
cards.short_summary: A specialized block off North Pleasant Street known for its community services and upscale dining.
cards.evidence_claim: Boltwood Walk is the location of Johnny's Tavern and the Bangs Community Center.
cards.source_title: Bangs Community Center | Amherst, MA - Official Website
cards.access_notes: Pedestrian-accessible block; community center hours vary.

cards.title: The Coffee and Cinema Block
cards.subtitle: Spring Street Corridor
cards.notes: Catch an indie film at Amherst Cinema or grab a specialty latte at Amherst Coffee.
cards.short_summary: A cultural block home to the town's independent movie theater and popular student study spots.
cards.evidence_claim: Spring Street is the location of Amherst Cinema and Amherst Coffee.
cards.source_title: About | Amherst Cinema
cards.access_notes: Public street; Amherst Cinema offers free tickets to Amherst College students.

cards.title: The Library Link
cards.subtitle: Amity Street Corridor
cards.notes: Walk down Amity to reach the Jones Library, a favorite off-campus study spot for students.
cards.short_summary: A residential and civic street connecting the downtown core to the town's main public library.
cards.evidence_claim: Amity Street is the location of the Jones Library, which serves as a community and student resource.
cards.source_title: About the Library | Jones Library
cards.access_notes: Public street; library hours vary by day.

cards.title: The Village Connector
cards.subtitle: Triangle Street Corridor
cards.notes: Use this route to connect between the downtown center and the North Amherst residential areas.
cards.short_summary: A diagonal street providing a key transit link between the town center and northern neighborhoods.
cards.evidence_claim: Triangle Street serves as a connector between the main downtown area and North Amherst residential zones.
cards.source_title: Amherst Zoning Map
cards.access_notes: Public street accessible 24/7.

cards.title: The Route 9 Gateway
cards.subtitle: Northampton Road (Route 9) Corridor
cards.notes: Follow this road west to find the Ginger Garden restaurant or to travel toward Northampton.
cards.short_summary: The western extension of Route 9 featuring suburban-style dining and transit to neighboring towns.
cards.evidence_claim: Northampton Road (Route 9) is home to businesses like Ginger Garden and serves as the main route to Northampton.
cards.source_title: Ginger Garden | Amherst Area Chamber of Commerce
cards.access_notes: Public highway; business hours vary.

cards.title: The Eastern Corridor
cards.subtitle: College Street (Route 9) Corridor
cards.notes: Walk east from campus to reach the Emily Dickinson Museum and the historic Homestead.
cards.short_summary: The eastern portion of Route 9 that borders the northern edge of the Amherst College campus.
cards.evidence_claim: College Street is the location of the Emily Dickinson Museum and the Homestead.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit | Emily Dickinson Museum
cards.access_notes: Public street; museum grounds are visible from the sidewalk.

cards.title: The Transit Link
cards.subtitle: University Drive Corridor
cards.notes: A major route for PVTA buses connecting Amherst College to the UMass campus and local shopping.
cards.short_summary: A primary north-south transit corridor used by students to navigate between the local colleges.
cards.evidence_claim: University Drive is a key route for the PVTA bus system and connects to major campus residential areas.
cards.source_title: Route 38 Schedule | PVTA
cards.access_notes: Public street; PVTA bus service is free for students with ID.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: From a nomadic bronze nymph to handcrafted walking sticks, Amherst College maintains a collection of rituals that define its unique liberal arts culture and history.

cards.title: The Nomadic Nymph
cards.subtitle: A 300-pound bronze statue of a water nymph
cards.notes: Compete for possession of this bronze nymph, a tradition of interclass rivalry where the statue is hidden and revealed in elaborate pranks.
cards.short_summary: A bronze statue that has been the subject of a century-long game of hide-and-seek between even-year and odd-year classes.
cards.evidence_claim: The Sabrina statue, a 300-pound bronze nymph donated in 1857, is the center of a long history of rivalry and pranks between student classes.
cards.source_title: Sabrina, Past & Present | Coeducation History & Timeline
cards.access_notes: The statue's location is traditionally kept secret by the class currently in possession of it.

cards.title: The Graduation Walking Sticks
cards.subtitle: Handcrafted beechwood canes for every graduate
cards.notes: Receive a handcrafted wooden cane at Commencement, a revived 19th-century custom symbolizing the enduring bond between the college and its alumni.
cards.short_summary: A unique Commencement tradition where every graduating senior is presented with a personalized wooden walking stick.
cards.evidence_claim: Since 2003, every graduating senior has received a handcrafted wooden cane, known as the Conway Cane, during the Commencement ceremony.
cards.source_title: Conway Canes: A Tradition for All | Alumni
cards.access_notes: Distributed annually during the Commencement ceremony on the main quad.

cards.title: The Battle for Housing
cards.subtitle: A high-stakes performance in Johnson Chapel
cards.notes: Perform a choreographed routine in Johnson Chapel to win the first pick in the campus housing lottery, a high-energy student favorite.
cards.short_summary: A competitive talent show where students perform lip-sync routines to secure top-tier dormitory rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: The Lip Sync competition is an annual event where student groups compete for the first pick in the housing selection process.
cards.source_title: Lip Sync 2025: Pitch Perfect Performances Compete for Housing
cards.access_notes: Held annually in Johnson Chapel; open to all students to watch or participate.

cards.title: The Spontaneous Holiday
cards.subtitle: A surprise day off for outdoor exploration
cards.notes: Wait for the surprise announcement of a day without classes to hike local peaks, a tradition dating back to the 19th century.
cards.short_summary: A floating autumn holiday where classes are canceled to encourage students to enjoy the outdoors and hike nearby mountains.
cards.evidence_claim: Amherst College has a historical tradition of Mountain Day, formally established in 1874 as a floating holiday for outdoor retreat.
cards.source_title: Mountain Day - The Consecrated Eminence
cards.access_notes: Announced spontaneously by the administration during the fall semester.

cards.title: The Final Gathering
cards.subtitle: A formal faculty tribute to graduates
cards.notes: Attend this traditional ceremony in Johnson Chapel where faculty honor graduating seniors with prizes and honorary class memberships.
cards.short_summary: A formal end-of-year ceremony where the faculty celebrates the achievements of the graduating class.
cards.evidence_claim: Senior Assembly is a traditional ceremony held after classes end, where faculty honor graduating students in Johnson Chapel.
cards.source_title: Senior Assembly | Information for Graduating Students
cards.access_notes: Held in Johnson Chapel; typically requires academic regalia for participants.

cards.title: The Harvest Celebration
cards.subtitle: A community festival at Book & Plow Farm
cards.notes: Enjoy live music and local food at the annual festival celebrating the college's on-campus farm and the Pioneer Valley harvest.
cards.short_summary: An annual autumn festival featuring food, music, and activities at the college's Book & Plow Farm.
cards.evidence_claim: Farm Fest is an annual event hosted by the Campus Activities Board and Book & Plow Farm, featuring live music and local harvests.
cards.source_title: Student Engagement & Leadership | Campus Activities Board
cards.access_notes: Held at Book & Plow Farm; open to the entire campus community.

cards.title: The Orientation Skits
cards.subtitle: A theatrical welcome for first-year students
cards.notes: Watch upperclassmen perform skits based on the admissions essays of the incoming class, a humorous introduction to campus life.
cards.short_summary: A traditional orientation performance where student actors dramatize excerpts from the new class's application essays.
cards.evidence_claim: Voices of the Class has been part of New Student Orientation since 2007, using excerpts from incoming students' admissions essays.
cards.source_title: 'This Has Gone Way Too Far': Videos Show Bizarre Sexual Ceremony
cards.access_notes: Performed in Johnson Chapel during first-year orientation week.

cards.title: The Graduation Curse
cards.subtitle: A campus myth about the War Memorial
cards.notes: Avoid walking directly on the War Memorial to ensure you graduate on time, a common superstition among the student body.
cards.short_summary: A student superstition that walking on the campus War Memorial will prevent a student from graduating.
cards.evidence_claim: A traditional superstition at Amherst involves avoiding walking on the war memorial to protect one's ability to graduate.
cards.source_title: Seeing Double: Tradition, Tradition!
cards.access_notes: The memorial is located on the south side of the main quad.

cards.title: The Civil War Chimes
cards.subtitle: A solitary steeple's musical tribute
cards.notes: Listen for the nine bells of Stearns Steeple, which are rung on special occasions to commemorate alumni who served in the Civil War.
cards.short_summary: The ringing of bells in a standalone church steeple to mark significant college events and honor historical figures.
cards.evidence_claim: Stearns Steeple contains nine bells cast in 1871, which are rung on suitable occasions to commemorate Civil War dead.
cards.source_title: Feature: The First War Memorial | 2009: Winter
cards.access_notes: The steeple is located between James Dormitory and the Mead Art Museum.

cards.title: The January Break
cards.subtitle: A three-week period of non-traditional learning
cards.notes: Participate in quirky workshops and community events during the January break, a time for students to explore interests outside the curriculum.
cards.short_summary: A three-week period in January dedicated to non-credit courses, workshops, and community-building activities.
cards.evidence_claim: Interterm is a three-week period in January where the Office of Student Engagement provides various programs and events.
cards.source_title: Student Engagement & Leadership | Interterm
cards.access_notes: Occurs annually during the month of January.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Amherst College, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A guide to the essential first-year experiences at Amherst College, from orientation traditions to exploring the campus landscape.

cards.title: Check In and Get Your Key
cards.subtitle: Friday Morning Arrival
cards.notes: Start your journey by picking up your room key at the First-Year Quad across from Frost Library. You will also receive your official Amherst class hoodie here.
cards.short_summary: The primary arrival and check-in point for new students to receive keys and orientation materials.
cards.evidence_claim: New students pick up room keys at the First-Year Quad across from Frost Library and receive a special Amherst class hoodie during orientation.
cards.source_title: Important To Dos | Information for New Students - Amherst College
cards.access_notes: Open for scheduled arrival windows during orientation week.

cards.title: First Meal at 'Val'
cards.subtitle: Friday Lunch
cards.notes: Head to the main dining commons, affectionately known as Val, for your first campus meal. It serves as the central social hub for the student body.
cards.short_summary: The primary dining facility at Amherst College, offering locally sourced produce from the campus farm.
cards.evidence_claim: Valentine Hall is the main dining facility, often called 'Val' by students, and offers continuous dining during the academic year.
cards.source_title: Valentine Hall | Dining Location Hours - Amherst College
cards.access_notes: Open daily; breakfast starts at 7:30 AM and dinner ends at 8:30 PM during the academic year.

cards.title: Sunset at the War Memorial
cards.subtitle: Friday Evening
cards.notes: Walk to the War Memorial for a panoramic view of the Holyoke Range. It is considered one of the most beautiful and meaningful spots on campus.
cards.short_summary: A scenic overlook and memorial offering expansive views of the surrounding Pioneer Valley landscape.
cards.evidence_claim: Memorial Hill provides panoramic views of the Holyoke Range and is described as the most beautiful spot on campus.
cards.source_title: The War Memorial: “A place of dignity and repose that stops you in your tracks.”
cards.access_notes: Outdoor space accessible 24/7.

cards.title: Explore the Mammoth Exhibits
cards.subtitle: Saturday Morning
cards.notes: Visit the museum to see over 1,700 specimens, including the iconic mammoth skeleton. It is staffed by student docents and is free to all.
cards.short_summary: A natural history museum featuring significant collections of fossils, minerals, and dinosaur footprints.
cards.evidence_claim: The Beneski Museum offers free admission and features three floors of exhibits including fossil skeletons and dinosaur footprints.
cards.source_title: Beneski Museum of Natural History | Plan a Visit - Amherst College
cards.access_notes: Open Saturday and Sunday from 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM.

cards.title: Connect at the Hub
cards.subtitle: Saturday Afternoon
cards.notes: Stop by Keefe to find student organization offices, the movie theater, and Schwemm's Coffeehouse. It is the center for student engagement.
cards.short_summary: The central student union building housing resource centers, a theater, and social spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Keefe Campus Center houses the Office of Student Activities, resource centers, a movie theater, and Schwemm's Coffeehouse.
cards.source_title: Keefe Campus Center | Our Community - Amherst College
cards.access_notes: Main campus center hours typically extend into the evening for student events.

cards.title: View the Global Collection
cards.subtitle: Saturday Late Afternoon
cards.notes: Browse over 20,000 objects in the Mead's collection. Admission is free, and it often hosts student-led tours and creative workshops.
cards.short_summary: The college's art museum featuring a diverse global collection spanning thousands of years.
cards.evidence_claim: The Mead Art Museum offers free public admission and houses a collection of over 20,000 objects.
cards.source_title: Mead Art Museum - Amherst College
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday through Sunday; check website for seasonal hours.

cards.title: Late Night at Val
cards.subtitle: Saturday Night
cards.notes: Join the tradition of 'Late Night' for snacks and socializing. It is a popular weekend activity for students staying on campus.
cards.short_summary: A late-night dining tradition at Valentine Hall offering snacks and a social atmosphere.
cards.evidence_claim: Late Night at Val runs Sunday through Thursday from 9:00 PM to 11:00 PM during the academic year.
cards.source_title: Dining Location Menus | Amherst College
cards.access_notes: Late night service typically runs 9:00 PM - 11:00 PM on select nights.

cards.title: Morning Hike on the Trails
cards.subtitle: Sunday Morning
cards.notes: Explore 500 acres of woods and wetlands. The trail network is perfect for a quiet morning walk or run away from the campus center.
cards.short_summary: A large nature preserve owned by the college featuring diverse ecosystems and a network of walking trails.
cards.evidence_claim: The Wildlife Sanctuary consists of 500 acres of woods, fields, and trails used for recreation and research.
cards.source_title: Wildlife Sanctuary | Town & Valley - Amherst College
cards.access_notes: Open to the public for daylight use.

cards.title: Visit the Campus Farm
cards.subtitle: Sunday Afternoon
cards.notes: Walk up to the farm to see where your dining hall produce is grown. Students can participate in pick-your-own flowers during the late summer.
cards.short_summary: An on-campus farm that provides fresh produce to the dining hall and serves as an educational resource.
cards.evidence_claim: Book & Plow Farm supplies Valentine dining hall and offers pick-your-own flower gardens for the campus community.
cards.source_title: Book & Plow Farm | Sustainability - Amherst College
cards.access_notes: The farm is open to the campus community; check for specific event times.

cards.title: Sunday Night Study Session
cards.subtitle: Sunday Evening
cards.notes: Prepare for your first week of classes at Frost Library. The Frost Café on the first floor is a popular spot for a caffeine boost while studying.
cards.short_summary: The main research library on campus, offering various study environments and a café.
cards.evidence_claim: Frost Library is the main library on campus and includes the Frost Café, which offers beverages and snacks.
cards.source_title: Library | Amherst College
cards.access_notes: Academic year hours typically include late night Sunday openings.
